items.title: JEPA challenges next-token scaling
items.oneliner: LeCun's JEPA paper claims aligned views beat next-token prediction, a direct shot at how multimodal foundation models get built.

items.title: Small model teams beat flagship coding models
items.oneliner: Five Qwen3.8-27B agents reportedly beat Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard, suggesting orchestration can outrun brute model size.

items.title: Framework choice now has token costs
items.oneliner: JavaScript frameworks now carry measurable AI tax in tokens, time, and accessibility debt, so DX vibes are no longer enough.

items.title: Critical Linux TCP bug needs patching
items.oneliner: A Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free scored 9.8 CVSS, giving remote attackers a serious path into unpatched servers.

items.title: A court punished prompt injection
items.oneliner: A Brazilian court fined lawyers about $16,000 for hidden prompt injection, turning AI misuse in filings into enforceable precedent.

items.title: Air-gapped machines can leak via RAM
items.oneliner: Researchers exfiltrated data from air-gapped computers through RAM-generated radio signals at 1000 bits per second.

items.title: Cities are physically unplugging AI surveillance
items.oneliner: A police chief unplugged Flock cameras after contract cancellation stalled, showing AI surveillance backlash is moving from debate to action.

items.title: KDE launched a GPU terminal
items.oneliner: KDE's new Kwi terminal claims 3x to 35x gains over Konsole, making GPU-accelerated terminals look practical.

items.title: Battery fleets are perturbing power grids
items.oneliner: Researchers traced one-minute grid frequency dips to synchronized battery state checks, a new coordination problem for electrified infrastructure.

items.title: A Rust difftool targets multimodal repos
items.oneliner: OmniDiff promises sub-100ms, content-aware diffs across code, images, and documents, which fits how modern repos actually look.
